The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

An AI label alone no longer wins lenders, JPMorgan says. As default insurance on several AI-linked firms hits record costs, companies must show they can finance investment, service the debt and eventually mint cash, JPMorgan says. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Solana bug reports now cost 1 SOL as AI floods security teams with spam. Researchers must now permanently burn 1 SOL for every submission after a monthlong contest drew 809 reports, with AI believed to have helped generate or write nearly all of them. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Ethereum fixes Glamsterdam bug that could have sent staking deposits to builders. Developers initially rejected the change before reversing course, as testing delays gave them more time to examine a flaw in Ethereum's upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Zcash co-founder proposes ending grants funding, citing $125 million treasury. Sean Bowe’s proposal would send the committee’s 8% share of newly created ZEC to a reserve for future miners. The committee would keep the money it has already received. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Ripple gets a final go-ahead to launch its own U.S. national trust bank. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency has approved Ripple National Trust Bank (RNTB), Ripple's CEO Brad Garlinghouse announced on X. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Tom Lee's Bitmine favors share buybacks to ether purchases as crypto declines. The Ethereum treasury firm spent $46 million buying back shares as Chairman Tom Lee said crypto has held up better than AI stocks during the recent market pullback. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $79,681 with a -0.60% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,309.82 with a -0.49% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Live markets: Bitcoin and ether ETFs drew inflows Monday
items.description:
U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs pulled in $265.69 million on Monday, the largest daily inflow in over a month and the second in three sessions after July 2 broke a long run of outflows, per SoSoValue data. Ether ETFs added $20.66 million the same day, led by BlackRock's ETHA at $23.29 million.

BlackRock's IBIT absorbed $209.40 million of the bitcoin total, with ARKB taking in $32.98 million and Grayscale's mini BTC fund adding $42.25 million. GBTC shed $44.45 million, the only fund in the red. [...] The daily turn has not fixed the weekly picture yet. Spot bitcoin ETFs still lost a net $526.6 million over the shortened holiday week, an eighth straight week of negative flows. Ether ETFs lost $13.7 million on the week.

Total bitcoin ETF assets climbed back to $77.32 billion from a June 30 low of $70.95 billion, helped by both the price recovery and the returning bid. Bitcoin traded near $63,200 as the data landed, per CoinDesk data.

Image 19

Latest Crypto News [...] Micron, Intel, AMD, Applied Materials, SanDisk and KLA Corp. are among the names that are lower by 9%-12%.

That, in turn, is pressuring crypto prices, with bitcoin dipping to $62,900 after having risen above $64,000 overnight. Bitcoin, however, is still higher by 1.2% over the past 24 hours.

Ether is higher by 1% over the last day, while XRP has turned negative by 1% over that time frame.

items.title: Ethereum ETFs Outpace Bitcoin ETFs in 2026 Inflows
items.description:
Ethereum ETF inflows into U.S. spot Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH) funds reached approximately $1.5 billion, surpassing the $985 million that spot Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) ETFs brought in. This data, sourced from SoSoValue, shows daily crypto ETF inflows and outflows. Spot ETFs directly hold the coins, so their share prices rise and fall with the cryptocurrency's market value. [...] Ethereum ETFs pulled in $1.5B in 2026 inflows, topping Bitcoin's $985M, yet Bitcoin ETFs still hold $109B in total assets, a figure roughly six times greater.
 Bitcoin ETFs staged a massive Q3 recovery, attracting $6.3 billion after $5 billion in net outflows during the first half of 2026.
 Ethereum is outpacing Bitcoin's inflow rate by $525M annually, but closing Bitcoin's $44B cumulative lead would still take over 80 years. [...] Over the years, Bitcoin ETFs have collected a staggering $57.6 billion in net inflows since their inception, whereas Ethereum funds have garnered $13.8 billion. Bitcoin ETFs began trading in January 2024—about six months before Ethereum funds, which debuted in July 2024.

At the current inflow rate, Ethereum funds are outpacing Bitcoin funds by about $525 million annually. However, it would take more than 80 years to close the existing $44 billion gap in total inflows.

items.title: Cryptocurrency regulation: U.S. laws and global developments
items.description: Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it's an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight. [...] Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. That splintered approach began to change in 2025, when Congress established a federal framework for stablecoins. Broader regulation of digital asset markets remains unsettled, although Congress and federal regulators have taken steps toward clarifying which assets and activities fall under securities or commodities

items.title: US Crypto Policy Tracker Regulatory Developments
items.description:
On April 4, 2025, the SEC’s Division of Corporation Finance (the Staff) published a Statement on Stablecoins clarifying that in the Staff’s view the offer and sale of certain dollar-backed stablecoins does not involve an offer and sale of securities requiring registration under the US federal securities laws (the Stablecoin Statement). The Stablecoin Statement specifically addresses stablecoins that are designed to maintain a stable value relative to the US dollar (USD) on a one-for-one basis, [...] On December 16, 2025, the FDIC issued a notice of proposed rulemaking (the Proposal) to implement Section 5 of the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for US Stablecoins Act (GENIUS Act). The GENIUS Act, enacted by Congress in July 2025, created a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins whereby a subsidiary of an insured depository institution could be approved to issue payment stablecoins.

Read more on Latham’sGlobal Fintech & Digital Assets Blog. items.title: 2025 Crypto Regulatory Round-Up
items.description:
What is the GENIUS Act and how does it regulate stablecoins?

The GENIUS Act is United States legislation passed in 2025 that establishes a federal regulatory framework for stablecoin issuers. It mandates strict requirements for reserve backing, audits, and financial integrity. The law also places restrictions on the domestic offering of foreign issued stablecoins, prompting a global acceleration in stablecoin policy development. [...] National regulators that have not yet developed or implemented stablecoin regulation will continue to make progress. By July 2026, U.S. federal and state regulators are required to promulgate final regulations to implement the GENIUS Act. This will include processes to license and regulate federal stablecoin issuers, and establishing criteria that foreign stablecoin issuers must meet in order to offer their stablecoins in the U.S. In Singapore, draft legislation to implement a stablecoin regime [...] Throughout the region, regulators are paying much closer attention to the systemic role of stablecoins — particularly their use in cross‑border payments, trade settlement, and inflation hedging — and are starting to define clearer requirements around issuance, reserve backing, redemption rights, and intermediary obligations, with FATF alignment and upcoming mutual evaluations serving as a common anchor for AML/CFT expectations and supervisory priorities.

items.title: Crypto Regulation in 2026: What Changed and What’s Ahead
items.description:
Regulatory trends

Stablecoin legislation

In July 2025, President Donald Trump signed the GENIUS Act legislation into law, requiring stablecoins to be backed 1-to-1 by the US dollar or other low-risk assets. The United States has also enacted the Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act, which prohibits Federal Reserve banks from establishing or issuing a US CBDC.

SEC and CFTC crypto clarity [...] Hong Kong has introduced a dedicated stablecoin issuer licensing regime under the HKMA and FSTB. It proposes high-quality reserve-asset backing, segregation and custody requirements, independent audits, clear redemption rights, and governance standards. Algorithmic stablecoins and unbacked arrangements will face restrictions.

ETF & tokenized-asset guidelines [...] Stablecoin payment rules in the UK are still in development and have not yet come into force. The government has outlined a future framework in which stablecoins used for payments would be subject to requirements on backing, redemption, and issuer governance, with payment-system regulators gaining expanded supervisory powers over systemic arrangements. items.title: Fed rate decision: Warsh faces a market on edge as Bitcoin sits at $79K, Gold weakens
items.description:
Markets enter FED day with a combination of optimism and caution. Global equities are green across the board, crypto is stabilizing after last week’s slide, commodities are mixed, and FX majors are drifting in narrow ranges. Beneath this calm surface sits a market fully aware that Kevin Warsh’s rate decision and tone today will dictate the next macro chapter. [...] ## Conclusion: Warsh’s tone will decide everything

Today is not about the rate number — it is about Warsh’s tone.

Markets are positioned for:

If Warsh leans hawkish, yields will rise, the dollar will strengthen, and Bitcoin’s $79K support will be tested.

If Warsh leans dovish, tech will extend gains, gold will rebound, and crypto will attempt a breakout.

If Warsh stays neutral, markets will chop violently before choosing direction.

# Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP Price Predictions Today: Why Is Crypto Falling?

CoinGabbar

CoinGabbar@coin\_gabbar\_6 min read

The crypto market took a step back today. The total market cap fell to $2.76 trillion, down 0.60% in the past 24 hours. Trading volume sits at $94.41 billion.

Bitcoin slipped to $78,062.80. Ethereum eased to $2,470.13. XRP dropped to $1.38. Most coins are red today, but the drop is mild, not a crash.

### Why is Crypto Market Down Today? [...] Ethereum trades at $2,472.04 today, down 1.80%. The coin has been stuck between $2,400 and $2,550 for over a week now.

Retail selling and a slowdown in demand from bigger buyers seem to be the main reasons for the sideways action.

Near-term resistance sits around $2,520 to $2,530. That level has rejected price several times in recent weeks. Each retest without a sharp rejection tends to weaken resistance over time, which raises the odds of an eventual breakout. [...] Markets are now pricing in a 60.4% chance of a rate hike at the September 16 Fed meeting, up from 39.6% odds of no change.

A month ago, the odds were close to a coin flip. Now, the market thinks a hike is more likely than not. Higher rates usually mean less money flowing into risk assets like crypto.

### Is the crypto market in fear or greed right now?

The Fear & Greed Index shows a score of 69 today. That puts the market in Greed territory.
